verdicts.reasoning: The fault is real, but 300 m is more buffer than the evidence needs. I computed each cell's distance to the nearest LST-NaN pixel and regressed LST on the land-cover and focal features. The residual is -1.73 to -1.97 °C at 0-60 m, -0.95 to -1.10 at 60-120 m and -0.40 to -0.49 at 120-240 m. The dTa residual in the same bins is about 0 (-0.07 to +0.13), so the air is not cooler there: the LST is contaminated, consistent with TIRS's 100 m pixels and edges just outside the shadow mask. Part of the reviewer's gradient is geographic, though. Measured within 2 km blocks, the edge bias is -0.75 to -0.95 at 0-60 m, -0.32 to -0.35 at 60-120 m and only -0.04 to -0.06 at 120-240 m. I also cannot reproduce +1.04 / +1.10 at 0.5-2 km; I get +0.5 at 0.5-1 km and 0 to +0.28 at 1-2 km. r(dTa, LST) matches the reviewer: 0.39-0.58 within 150 m and 0.53-0.67 beyond 300 m. A 150 m buffer already gives r of 0.54 / 0.64 / 0.63 and keeps 80-83% of LST cells, while 300 m keeps only 62-67% (38-43% of driven cells). The contamination is noise in B's predictor and is uncorrelated with dTa, so it works against finding a B-A gain rather than for it. A and B are scored on the same cells, so the cloud selection does not bias B-A. Keeping the city is right.
verdicts.recommended_action: Keep the city. Dilate the QA cloud mask before masking LST, but by about 150 m (5 cells) rather than 300 m. Dilate only the cloud, dilated_cloud, cirrus and cloud_shadow bits, not 'fill', so scene edges are not eaten. Keep the undilated mask for clear_fraction, record the buffer, and rebuild LST.

verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed for am. CAPA34 (both the N and S keys) is +1.369 and CAPA39 is -1.387, a two-vehicle component linked by 19 shared cells 52 minutes apart (dT 2.84, SD 0.05). Against fe drift only: r 0.933, RMS 0.49. I checked out of sample with near-simultaneous visits of different vehicles to nearby but different cells. The am offsets make agreement worse: within 1.5 km and 30 min the mean squared difference rises from 0.31 to 1.86. CAPA38-CAPA39 goes from -0.56 to -1.94 (5,122 pairs) and CAPA34-CAPA63 from -0.24 to -1.60 (6,585 pairs). The af offsets (CAPA39 -0.875, CAPA44 +0.941), however, are mostly corroborated: CAPA44-CAPA48 goes from +0.91 to -0.03 (1,221 pairs) and CAPA39-CAPA44 from -1.62 to +0.20 (1,675 pairs), so keeping af with its offsets is right. pm offsets are about 0. Neither proposed code fix works. The ridge as specified (lam = s2/0.09 = 5.3) still leaves CAPA34 / CAPA39 at about +1.0 / -1.1, because the link looks precise. The minimum-link rule would also zero the corroborated af offsets here and all of Richmond's.
verdicts.recommended_action: Exclude am (or rebuild am with CAPA47's warm-up cut and with no offsets for the CAPA34/CAPA39 component). Keep af and pm with their fe offsets. Do not adopt the ridge or the minimum-link rule as written. Instead, check offsets against near-simultaneous visits of different vehicles to nearby cells, or use those pairs as extra links. Leave offsets off for components of two vehicles joined by a single stretch.

verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed. S:CAPA47's 1-minute medians are a flat 23.9-24.2 °C from 06:04 to 06:14 over 7.2 km, then fall to 18.4 °C by 06:18. verdicts.reasoning: The numbers are right (af fe vs drift-only r 0.733, RMS 0.74; pm r 0.816, RMS 0.57), but the claim that the offsets are not sensor biases does not hold. The signs are consistent across the day: 1072 is +0.45 / +0.71 / +0.35, 1082 -0.26 / -1.29 / -0.41 and 1104 -0.24 / -0.89 / -0.20. 1094's am '0' only means it was not linked in am. The larger af values fit a sun-dependent shield error. I tested out of sample with near-simultaneous visits of different vehicles to nearby but different cells; these pairs are independent of the shared-cell links. The fe offsets halve the mismatch: af 0.70 to 0.44 (within 300 m and 10 min) and 1.92 to 0.95 (within 800 m and 20 min, 40,528 pairs); pm 1.07 to 0.36 and 1.17 to 0.60. Specific links are corroborated: 1094-1103 af goes from +1.35 to -0.42 (12,379 pairs), 1072-1082 af from +2.04 to +0.05 (2,208) and 1093-1094 pm from -0.68 to +0.08 (15,707). So excluding af is not warranted. pm has a local fault: 1102's -1.04 comes from a two-vehicle component {1088, 1102} joined by 7 cells 57 minutes apart, and nearby pairs contradict it (1094-1102 goes from -0.51 to -2.37 with 784 pairs; 1088-1102 from +0.95 to -0.92). That route holds 34% of the pm sum of squares. The proposed minimum-link rule (at least 30 shared cells within 10 min) would zero every Richmond offset, including the corroborated ones. The ridge halves them without telling good from bad.
verdicts.recommended_action: Keep am and af with their fe offsets. Exclude pm until a rebuild that sets 1102's offset to zero (or drops the offsets of the {1088, 1102} component). Do not adopt the minimum-link rule. Check offsets against near-simultaneous visits to nearby cells, or use those pairs as links, and leave offsets off for two-vehicle components joined by one short stretch.

verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed. In af, n_spread is 0 (233 cells revisited, none 15 or more minutes apart), so protocol is used. Sensors 1040, 1065, 1069 and 1074 (-75.98 to -76.07 E) stop at 15:26:51-15:27:00, and 1068 (-76.18 E, mean 34.2 °C) starts at 15:18. The 10-minute medians run from 31.6 to 34.1 °C. The protocol detrend weakens the coast-inland signal: r(dTa, lon) is -0.455 undetrended, -0.408 within-vehicle and -0.330 protocol, and r(dTa, LST) is 0.327, 0.313 and 0.282. The code fix is sound and general: it reduces to the current line when every vehicle runs the whole hour. am and pm use fe with offsets of at most 0.15 (RMS 0.06-0.08).

issues.evidence: fe is used in both runs (spread-revisit cells 97/66, drift SE 0.22 °C/h). The vehicle offsets span 3.42 °C (am) and 3.08 °C (af), e.g. CAPA1021 -2.22 and 1048 +1.85. These offsets are real sensor biases. The same sensor pairs differ by the same amount in both runs at shared cells: 1031-1036 by 1.58 °C (am, 29 cells, 6.9 min apart) and 1.53 °C (af, 26 cells, 4.6 min); 1048-CAPA1021 by 1.95 / 1.98 °C (7 cells each). After the fe correction, a check against neighbour cells within 150 m (other vehicles) leaves the linked sensors within ±0.3 °C (1031, 1048, CAPA1021, over 1152-1929 pairs). But the 11 am vehicles form 5 linked groups and the 17 af vehicles 7 groups, so unlinked vehicles keep their bias at offset 0. Example: sensor 1029 (af, 914 cells, about 6% of the run) reads 2.18 °C above its only neighbour, 1025 (48 pairs within 150 m, 4 min apart, 94% of pairs above 2 °C). In am, 1046 and CAPA1022 differ by 1.34 °C over 763 pairs.

Better: estimate one offset per sensor across am and af (11 sensor ids appear in both runs) and link vehicles through neighbour cells within about 100 m, not only identical cells. Alternatively drop sensor 1029 from af.

verdicts.reasoning: I rebuilt the per-visit frames with the build's own code path. They match meta exactly: fe drift +1.391 / -0.397 °C/h, SE 0.22, 97/66 spread-revisit cells, 5 and 7 linked groups, offset ranges 3.42 / 3.08 °C. The raw differences at shared cells reproduce: 1031-1036 is +1.58 °C (29 cells, 6.9 min) in am and +1.53 °C (26 cells, 4.6 min) in af; 1048-CAPA1021 is +1.95 / +1.98 °C (7 cells each). A sensor-pair bias that repeats across two runs is real, so 1.5-2 °C sensor biases exist. Single-vehicle groups get offset 0 by construction (1023B, 1032 and 1037 in am; 1029, 1037, 1043 and 1044 in af), so the structural point holds. The 1029 vs 1025 figure also reproduces (48 pairs within 150 m, +2.18 °C, 94% above 2 °C). But 150 m neighbour differences are not clean evidence of bias. Pairs inside the same linked group differ just as much: 1030-1048 +3.97 °C (26 pairs), 1031-CAPA1021 +1.97 °C at 1.4 min. In a leave-sensor-out land-cover model, linked sensors carry route residuals as large as the singletons (1048 af -1.67, 1032 af +1.84, 1025 af -1.37; singleton 1029 +1.02). The linking itself is weak in places: 1025-1031 share 1 cell, and the 1048/CAPA1021 pair links to the main group only through cells 40-54 min apart. Its offset relative to the others shifts about 1.85 °C between am and af, while 1031/1036/1025/1039 stay within about 0.15. This error is route-level noise that hits A and B alike, not an LST-specific bias. So keep-with-note is right and 'major' overstates it.
verdicts.recommended_action: Keep both runs, with a note in meta/QA: '5 (am) and 7 (af) unlinked vehicle groups; sensor biases up to about 2 °C are corrected only within groups; singletons and weakly linked groups carry route-level errors of about 1-2 °C (noise for A and B alike).' Do not drop sensor 1029: its 48-pair excess is within the spread of linked sensors after land-cover adjustment. Do not adopt neighbour-cell linking within 100-150 m as stated: it would build spatial differences of up to about 4 °C into the offsets. If cross-run sensor offsets are tried later, test them first; the 1048/CAPA1021 relative swing shows they do not simply carry over.

verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed from raw consecutive positions per vehicle. Farmville moves at median 4.7 / 5.4 / 5.7 km/h (p10-p90 about 3-7 km/h), with 1.3-1.6 m steps at 1 reading/s. Lynchburg the same day moves at 32-37 km/h with 9-10 m steps. Abingdon is also walked (4.9-5.0 km/h, 1.4 m steps). No other city has steps under 7 m (Boston's 0.0 m is a different artefact). My percentiles are slightly higher than the reviewer's (for example 62% of am readings below 5 km/h, not 78%), but the conclusion is the same. Runs cover 947-1317 cells within about 4 × 6 km, and af dTa SD 1.25 °C is the highest of the inland VFIC cities (0.60-1.08), as stated. A slow, poorly aspirated sensor in daytime sun can exaggerate sun/shade contrasts, which correlate with canopy and LST, so walked runs matter specifically for B − A. There is no direct proof of a radiation fault, so tag-and-sensitivity is the proportionate response, not exclusion. Abingdon has no clear Landsat scene, so evaluate_window already drops it from every LST-present window. In practice the with/without run only changes Farmville.
verdicts.recommended_action: Keep Farmville, tag it as a pedestrian campaign, and report the B − A (and C − A) verdict with and without it; Abingdon is already out of LST-present windows. Add the platform check in sparc/core/lstair/dataset.py build_city as proposed: per run, the median speed from each vehicle's consecutive raw points (dt ≤ 30 s), stored as qa['median_speed_kmh'], with a warning below 10 km/h. Cars are ≥ about 30 km/h, so the threshold separates cleanly.

verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed. Bicycle_CAPA56 appears in all three car files with 760 / 680 / 704 cells, sharing 0 / 0 / 6 of them with cars. Its cells have median canopy 67-75% (cars 0-6%), impervious 8-25% (cars 75-81%) and lie 163-247 m from water. In pm its cells have median dTa -3.14 °C (p5 -6.49) and make up 98% of the 293 cells with |dTa| > 5. Within 150 m of CAPA20 it reads -4.58 °C (pm, 17 min) and -2.25 °C (am, 14 pairs). Without it, pm SD drops from 1.63 to 1.23. The innocent explanation is partly true: cold air on the American River Parkway in the evening is plausible physics. But it is a different platform (lower, slower sensor) sampling an off-street domain that no other city's target contains. The bicycle files in Burlington, Las Cruces and New Orleans were skipped only because CAPA published them normalised to 0-1 with no temperature. So dropping it makes the target uniform (street-level traverses), and in pm it would otherwise dominate Sacramento's held-out MSE. The 'exclude pm' fallback is heavier than needed. The bike cells are disjoint from car cells, and the protocol drift barely moves without them (am 0.919 to 0.913, af 0.873 to 0.750, pm -3.27 to -3.17 °C/h). A full rebuild without the bike gives pm SD 1.23 / p1 -3.30, against 1.23 / -3.19 from simply dropping its rows; evaluate.recentre_target already re-centres on scored cells.

If no rebuild is possible, drop the bike-only rows from table.parquet rather than excluding the pm run; the result is nearly identical. Apply the code fix in build_city, but match on the sensor id (the part of vehicle_key after the last ':'), not the whole key with its folder path, and log what was dropped. So 09-23 am is a make-up drive for that route's missing morning window, not a fragment. 09-21 covers a route nobody drove on 09-18 (CAPA73 has only 2 readings in the 09-18 pm). The 0.1 C quantisation averaged over about 3 readings per cell gives about 0.02 C of noise, far below the SD of 0.11-0.25. Each run's dTa is centred on its own median, and evaluate.py centres predictions per (slug, run_id), so a single-route run is a valid within-run anomaly test and adds no bias to B-A. The cells without LST on 09-23 simply drop out of the A/B comparison, which uses the same cells for both.

concerns.title: The B − A statistic and the A/B training loss both use absolute °C² MSE, so one high-variance city (LA) decides the result
concerns.evidence: Code: evaluate.py:172-176 (_weights) gives each city equal weight by cell count but not by variance. evaluate.py:278-279 (the inner CV) averages per-city MSE, and evaluate.py:545-553 (paired) takes mean ΔMSE and rel = mean/mean(MSE_A) over absolute MSE. The spread of dTa SD across cities is large: af 0.44 (Austin) to 3.50 (LA); am up to 2.99 (San Bernardino), 1.90 (Seattle), 1.88 (Sedona); pm up to 2.06 (LA), 1.82 (Virginia Beach). Evidence from the existing af smoke evaluation (scratchpad/smoke_eval, 7 cities, same city caches with identical built_utc): LA's ΔMSE(B−A) is −3.82 out of a summed −4.22, i.e. 90% of the reported mean of −0.603 and the −16% relative change. The other 6 cities average −0.067. Only 3 cities improve and 4 get worse, and the mean per-city relative ΔMSE is +3.3%, so B is worse on average. LA also contaminates training: it holds about 71% of the equal-weighted squared loss (var 12.3 against 0.2-1.6). Refitting the selected ridge (α=300) with and without LA in training (qa_work/completeness/la_dom.py) gives: Asheville A r −0.21 → +0.54, MSE 1.685 → 0.910, B−A −0.353 → −0.074; Seattle A r −0.21 → +0.18, B−A −0.489 → −0.178; Austin A MSE 0.436 → 0.223. So much of the 'LST gain' in other cities is B undoing an LA-learned elevation artefact, since LA af has r(dTa, elev) +0.81 against −0.49 in Asheville. With variance-equalised weights (LA kept), mean B−A falls from −0.603 to −0.199, and to −0.041 without LA. The inner CV picked α=300, the top of the grid, in 6 of 7 folds; its inner MSE of 3.3-9 °C² is LA-sized.
concerns.recommended_check: Rerun with (i) training weights 1/(n_city·var_city(dTa)), which uses training labels only, or a per-city standardised target. (ii) Run the paired test on a scale-free per-city statistic as well: ΔMSE/MSE_A or ΔMSE/var(dTa), plus a Wilcoxon test. (iii) Do a leave-one-group-out influence analysis of the verdict (drop LA, San Diego, San Bernardino, Seattle in turn). Report the verdict under absolute and relative weighting. Exclude or flag runs whose dTa SD is near sensor noise (Fort Lauderdale make-up runs: SD 0.11-0.25), so relative statistics are not dominated by noise. Extend ridge_alphas beyond 300.

concerns.title: No null model: A is worse than predicting zero in several held-out cities, so 'beats A' can mean 'is less wrong'
concerns.evidence: Smoke af run (predictions.parquet; MSE of the zero prediction, i.e. the target variance, against A): Asheville 1.20 vs A 1.685 (r −0.21); Austin 0.196 vs 0.436 (r −0.07); LA 12.36 vs 20.01 (r −0.87); Seattle 1.65 vs 2.44 (r −0.21). In LA, B 'improves' by 3.8 °C² while still anti-correlated (r −0.70); it only has a smaller spread (SD 0.68 vs 0.99). C − A wins 6 of 7 cities, partly through shrinkage: C's prediction SD is 0.23-0.51 against A's 0.24-0.99. In Austin, C (MSE 0.205) is worse than zero (0.196) yet counts as beating A by 0.23. The 5% relative-gain rule at evaluate.py:553/569 is measured against a baseline that is worse than no model. SplineTransformer(extrapolation="linear") at evaluate.py:150 lets out-of-range anomalies extrapolate; LA's elevation_c SD is 140 m against 6-46 m elsewhere.
concerns.recommended_check: Add a model N (predict 0 after centring) to evaluate_window. Report B − N and C − N with the same paired test, and require B and C to beat N before any claim. Report per window how many held-out cities have r(A, dTa) < 0. Add a scale-free comparison: paired difference in spatial r, or MSE after a training-derived amplitude calibration. Rerun A with extrapolation='constant' to see how much of A's deficit is extrapolation.

concerns.title: 'Land cover' in A is WorldCover class fractions, so B − A measures LST beyond a crude categorical map
concerns.evidence: features_open.py:7-8 and :242-244: canopy = WorldCover 2021 'tree' class fraction and impervious = 'built' class fraction. The classes are mutually exclusive per 10 m pixel, and the 2021 map is applied to 2019-2023 campaigns. On af driven cells, canopy is exactly 0 for 55-98% of cells in 17 of 31 cities: Houston 0.55, Boston 0.56, Providence 0.61 (median canopy 0, median impervious 91.7%), LA 0.72, New Orleans 0.80, San Diego 0.82, Albuquerque 0.92, Las Cruces 0.98. Among canopy = 0 cells, NDVI p90 is 0.40-0.50 in humid cities (New Orleans 0.50, Charleston 0.50, Houston 0.43, Asheville 0.86), so street trees and lawns inside 'built' pixels are invisible to canopy. LST picks up this sub-class shading and vegetation. A positive B − A would then mean 'beyond WorldCover', not 'beyond land cover'.
concerns.recommended_check: Every city is in CONUS, so rebuild A's canopy and impervious from continuous 30 m NLCD (USFS tree canopy cover and NLCD percent impervious of the nearest year), keep NDVI and albedo, and rerun B − A. Report how much of B's gain survives. At minimum, report B − A for cities where canopy = 0 on fewer than 40% of cells against the others.

concerns.title: LST may earn B's gain as a proxy for coast-to-inland and terrain gradients on large grids, not as surface-air coupling
concerns.evidence: The cities where B gains are those where dTa is driven by mesoscale gradients that land cover does not resolve. LA af: r(dTa, impervious) −0.006, r(dTa, elevation) +0.81, r(dTa, LST) +0.53, grid 42 x 49 km. Seattle af: r(dTa, impervious) −0.011 vs r(dTa, LST) +0.44, grid 56 x 68 km. San Diego af: −0.049 vs +0.38, grid 31 x 39 km. In the smoke run, the three B-better cities are LA, Seattle and Asheville; the four flatter, smaller-signal cities get worse. lst_c is the cell LST minus the run's median over the whole driven area (evaluate.py:128-131), so it carries regional gradients, e.g. the marine-layer-cooled coast at the 10:30 overpass. A's only regional terms are the within-run elevation anomaly and log water distance. These clear western scenes (clear fraction 0.98-1.0, small offsets) coincide with the high-variance runs, while humid eastern cities have cloudier, more offset scenes (Charleston 0.61, Lynchburg 0.52, Providence 0.55, Raleigh +16 d).
concerns.recommended_check: Split LST into a regional part (Gaussian focal at about 3-5 km) and a local residual (lst − lst_f3000). Rerun B with only the residual, and also add regional non-satellite controls to A (distance to coast, 3-5 km focal elevation and impervious). Stratify B − A by grid extent (< 30 km vs larger) and by coastal vs inland.

concerns.title: Physics fits sit at the L bounds, LST fits switch off the land-cover source, and the per-parameter median transfer mixes incompatible fits
concerns.evidence: Smoke af physics fits (smoke_eval/physics/*.json, physics_iter 30 vs default 60): L = 60 m, the floor of one 60 m cell from physics.py:415-418, for Atlanta, Raleigh and Seattle (both C and C0). L = 2000 m, the ceiling, for LA (C 2000, C0 1999). Only 3 of 7 lie inside the bounds (73-178 m). The transferred median L of about 100 m spreads the source over fewer than 2 cells, so C is close to a local fixed-form regression. In the LST fits, the land-cover gain collapses: a = 0.0093 vs 17.19 without LST (Austin), 0.0156 vs 1.52 (Seattle), 0.051 vs 13.8 (LA). Raleigh's g_lst is 3.5e-8 (c_lst at its floor). transfer_params (evaluate.py:428-437) takes separate medians of L, a_phys, g and e0-e3 over different cities, which gives a parameter set that no city fitted. Separately, physics.py:697 fills cells with no LST with the frame mean, so in cities with 30-46% LST NaN (Charleston, Lynchburg, Providence, Atlanta) the fit's LST term is attenuated in cloud gaps.
concerns.recommended_check: Per window, report the number of fits with L within 5% of L_lo or L_hi. Rerun C and C0 with physics_iter 60, physics_cell_m 30 (floor 30 m) and L_max 5000 m, then compare C − A. As a sensitivity, transfer a coherent parameter vector: the full fit of the median-loss training city, or one pooled fit over the training cities. Exclude bound-pinned fits from the medians. Fit C only on LST-covered cells (y = NaN elsewhere) and check whether g_lst and C − C0 change.

concerns.title: A's land-cover anomalies are centred before the LST filter, while LST and the target are centred after it
concerns.evidence: design() runs on all of a window's cells (evaluate.py:627; centring at :126-131). Cells without LST are dropped afterwards (:650), and the target is re-centred on the remaining cells (:659). So in cloudy cities the land-cover anomalies of the scored cells are not median-zero, while lst_c is. Medians over all driven cells vs scored cells (af): Seattle impervious 53.3 → 68.8, elevation 88 → 75 m; Charleston impervious 25 → 33, canopy 50 → 33; Lynchburg canopy 25.7 → 41.7; Salem impervious 33 → 42. Prediction centring removes a constant only for a linear model; with splines and GBM, the offset moves along the learned curve, and only LST is centred on the scored cells.
concerns.recommended_check: Apply the predictor filter before design(), so all anomalies use the scored cells, which uses positions only. Rerun B − A and check that per-city ΔMSE for Seattle, Charleston, Lynchburg, Providence, Atlanta and Salem does not change materially.

concerns.title: The fixed physics regime per window does not match the forcing in several cities (am 'day' at SW ≈ 0; pm 'night' with sun up)
concerns.evidence: WINDOW_REGIME (evaluate.py:360) makes am a day window. Yet ERA5 am SW is 0.0-10 W/m² in 10 cities (Atlanta 0.0, Fort Lauderdale 0.0, Austin 0.1, San Bernardino 0.2, Boise 0.4, Houston 1.4, Asheville 5.0, LA 5.1, Charleston 5.6, San Diego 10.0) against 197.5 in Sedona and 200.5 in Victorville. At SW ≈ 0 the shade, kc and albedo terms of Q* (physics.py:986-1000) have no influence, so their medians are effectively starting values, and these are transferred to the two SW-dominated cities. pm is a night window, but the sun is still up in the west: SW 209 in Salt Lake City, 179 in Boise, 144 in Seattle and Abingdon, 139 in Asheville, 130 in Salem.
concerns.recommended_check: Report C − A and C − C0 for am without Sedona and Victorville, and for pm split by SW < 50 vs ≥ 50 W/m². Alternatively, run both regimes for every window as a sensitivity, and report which parameters were identifiable (moved from their starting values) in each fit.

concerns.title: Per-window verdicts are tested separately at one-sided 0.025, with no primary window or correction
concerns.evidence: evaluate() (evaluate.py:781-786) runs af, am and pm (and ni where possible), and each window gets its own paired() verdict (B−A, C−A, C−C0) at ALPHA 0.025. cli.py:169-177 prints each window's verdict, with no rule for combining them. Claiming when any of the three windows passes inflates the error rate to about 7% under the null, and the windows share cities, so they are not independent evidence.
concerns.recommended_check: Name af as the primary window before running on the real data, or apply Holm across windows (and across B−A and C−A if both are claimed). Report the combined per-city statistic as a secondary result.
